## Triage: first grade confirmed (`bug` · `priority:p2`), routed `domain:services` · `area:access`, into `pm:queue` (`finding` removed). The projection keeps the owner the protocol read serves

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-13T11:02Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Why p2:** ADR-0090 D5's "packages suggest, admins confirm" silently does nothing for a runtime package's default set. Two framework reads also disagree about who owns the set. Measured on a real tenant kernel. Nothing is granted wrongly: the suggestion is simply missing.
- **Lane:** the permission-set projection is `plugin-security`'s, so `domain:services`.
- **Direction:**
  - The projection carries the package binding the publish door resolved (the one `protocol.getMetaItem` serves as `_packageId`) into `package_id` and the managed-by marker. A runtime package's `isDefault` set then records its suggestion.
  - ⛔ No second owner derivation.
  - **Pins:**
    - publish a runtime package's `isDefault` set without a body `packageId`: one suggestion row, and the catalog read and the protocol read name the same owner;
    - a code package's set is unchanged.

Claim: PM loop round 10 · 2026-10-13T11:17Z
Session: `session_01FzQy26KznSa5j2gnf3AzsE`
Account: `zhuangjianguo` (the seat's linked user as `GET /user` answers it; the card's assignee)
Branch: `claude/issue-23233-projection-keeps-package-owner`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-23233`
Domain: `domain:services`
Seat: `domain:services#2` (seat post #21118)
File surface: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-set-projection.ts` (the projection's echo and row: it carries the publish door's resolved package binding), its tests, and `suggested-audience-bindings.ts` only if the suggestion collector needs the carried owner. One `.changeset/23233-*.md`. `packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts` is read, not edited ("⛔ no second owner derivation") (stop on breach; explain in the report)
Container & model: `M (one owner carried through a projection, with suggestion and owner-agreement pins)`, `mode:subagent`, `model: default — dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack: "no path-derived mandate … The tier stays the PM's per-card judgment call"`
Clause-②: no — the projection keeps the package owner the protocol read already serves (ADR-0090 D5: packages suggest, admins confirm); no published schema or export moves. If the measurement finds that a package-managed row narrows what an admin may edit, the dev reports it and the line gains `(narrowing)`.
Responsibility: `plugin-security`'s permission-set projection (the platform's own code) strips `_packageId` from the echo it registers | none: the protocol read carries the owner, but the catalog and the suggestion collector read the stripped echo | every runtime package that publishes an `isDefault` set without a body `packageId`; measured on a real tenant kernel (objectstack-ai/cloud#2847)
Thread-read: 6144115478
Serial constraints cleared: none of the open PRs touches `permission-set-projection.ts`, `suggested-audience-bindings.ts` or `security-catalog.ts` (read at this claim). Their last landings are the C2/C3 epic's own stages (`c8a9783eca` stage 6b-2, `d112087b89` stage U2), so the files are the epic's territory in substance and are declared to #15194 before any edit.

PR #23311 (#23259) makes `plugin-security`'s `declaredOwnerOf` read the package binding only. Until it lands, a package-bound published permission set whose body declares an agreeing `packageId` is attributed correctly during the host-kernel write-through window (the set is registered without `_packageId` until the next list read), because the body-key fallback masks the window. After it lands, such a set waits for the next list read like every other set. The #23259 dev measured that window (probe B in the report on #23259). The cure stays this card's remainder, the write-through stamping `_packageId`; keeping the fallback until then was considered and declined on #23259.
